To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sensitivity of the North Atlantic Subpolar Gyre to surface wind stress is reversed between present-day and glacial climate, and that this reversal can be understood in terms of the dynamics of the deep water formation in the Nordic Seas.

the North Atlantic sub-polar gyre (hereafter the SPG) is a complex entity that can be decomposed in three distinct components, namely, an Ekman transport (ET), a thermohaline transport (THT) and a bottom transport (BT).
